description: SYNTHETIC sample posts written for Vantage demos and evaluation. They are NOT real posts and have no real authors or links. Each item carries the label a careful human would assign (expectedLabel) for the demo seller (Beacon Support; competitors Zendesk, Intercom). Dates are expressed as daysAgo so they stay recent.

items.text: We're a 12-person SaaS and support requests are scattered across Gmail, our chat widget and Twitter DMs. Things slip through the cracks every week. Looking for a helpdesk that isn't $50 per agent. What are you all using?
items.note: clear request with team size and pain

items.text: Our support inbox is a shared Google Group and it is collapsing. 4 people, maybe 60 tickets a day. Need something simple with canned replies and email plus chat in one place. Recommendations?
items.note: shared inbox outgrown, asks for recommendations

items.text: Zendesk renewal quote just came in at double what we paid last year. Is there anything that does tickets and a basic help center for a team of 8 without enterprise pricing? Evaluating Help Scout and Freshdesk but open to other ideas.
items.note: names competitor but is evaluating alternatives

items.text: Ask HN: What do you use for customer support at a 5-person startup? We've outgrown replying from a shared inbox and I don't want to spend a week configuring something heavy.

We need to pick a support tool before our launch next month. Priorities: shared inbox, simple automations and a Slack integration. Budget is about $200 a month in total. Any real-world experience to share?

Switching away from Intercom because the per-seat plus per-resolution pricing got out of hand. We are a B2B SaaS with about 300 customers. Has anyone moved to something cheaper that still does in-app chat?
items.note: switching away from a named competitor

items.text: Is there a self-hostable helpdesk that handles email tickets well? We're a small team and compliance wants the data in our own infrastructure. Looking at Zammad and a few others, would love opinions before we commit this quarter.

Founder here. Support is eating 15 hours a week of my time and I keep losing track of who replied to whom. What is a good lightweight ticketing setup for a solo founder plus one contractor? I need to fix this within a couple of weeks.
Our customers email, chat and message us on social and I have no single view of any of it. Which tool actually unifies these without a three-month rollout? Need something live within two weeks.
We're comparing Help Scout, Front and Freshdesk for a 20-person company. If you have used more than one, what surprised you after the first month?
Zendesk's admin UI is a maze. It took me two days to figure out how to add a simple trigger, and every small change seems to need a different add-on. We pay a lot for something this hard to use.
Intercom's pricing changed again and our bill jumped by about 40 percent. The product is fine but the way they bill makes budgeting impossible for a small team.
Zendesk's automation rules are very limited on our plan. Support told us the feature we need is only on the enterprise tier, which is a huge jump from what we pay now.
Another outage in Zendesk Support this morning and our team couldn't see any tickets for an hour. Third time this quarter. This is not acceptable for something we depend on every day.
Intercom's inbox keeps duplicating conversations when a customer replies from two email addresses. I reported it twice and still nothing. Is anyone else seeing this?
Spent a week migrating off Help Scout and the export was missing half the conversation history. Their docs say it is supported. Be careful if you are planning the same.
items.note: complaint about a helpdesk NOT in the seller's competitor list

items.text: Support tickets are the worst part of my job. Customers never include the information you need, and ticketing tools make it worse by forcing everyone through forms. I am so tired of this.
items.note: frustration with support workflows, no search for a tool

items.text: Our helpdesk tool's mobile app crashes every time I open an attachment. Why is it so hard to ship a stable app in 2026?
Every support tool wants me to buy an AI add-on now. I just want tickets and a shared inbox. Rant over.
items.note: frustration about AI add-ons in support tools

items.text: Handling angry customers all day with a clunky ticket system is burning me out. There has to be a better way but I don't have time to research anything right now.
items.note: burnout, explicitly no time to research

items.text: We built TicketNest, a $9 per agent alternative to Zendesk and Intercom with a free tier. Would love feedback from founders tired of enterprise pricing. Link in my profile.
Launching HelpPilot today: AI first-response for support teams. 14-day trial, no card needed. Happy to answer questions.
I used Zendesk at my last job and it was fine. Anyway, the real question is whether remote work actually improves productivity.
Ask HN: How do you stay focused while working from home with kids around?
Acme Cloud | Support Engineer | Remote | We use Zendesk and Slack day to day. Apply through the link in this post.
The potential for insanity goes through the roof when the dev team is cut off from the client and every requirement arrives through a project manager who relays it second hand.
items.note: frustration about development management, not support tools

items.text: I am skeptical that LLM agents will replace support teams any time soon. They still hallucinate policy details and customers notice immediately.
items.note: opinion about AI and support, no request or complaint
